svg.text: Four different teams, the same underlying answer: deterministic policy, outside the model
Meta — LlamaFirewall (Purple Llama, real, arXiv 2505.03574)
PromptGuard 2 (jailbreak detector) → Agent Alignment Checks (a chain-of-thought
auditor reading the agent's own reasoning for goal misalignment) → CodeShield
(static analysis before generated code executes).
Scope: content-safety, not authorization — answers "is this dangerous," not "is this agent allowed."
OpenAI — tool approvals + moderation pipeline
Separates prompt from tool execution; a synchronous moderation layer screens
input/output before a tool call is even generated; human-in-the-loop approval
is the default for higher-risk actions.
See the real July 2026 incident below — even this didn't stop a benchmark exploit chain.
Google — Vertex AI / Agent Development Kit
Tool calls are matched deterministically against a pre-defined OpenAPI schema —
a call that doesn't exactly match the schema is rejected by the API gateway itself,
not by asking the model to reconsider.
Same shape as JiMesh's OPA gate: the schema/policy check is code, not a second model call.
AWS — Bedrock AgentCore (2025)
AgentCore Identity brokers short-lived, per-agent STS credentials (AssumeRole +
a per-call session policy) instead of a standing IAM role; AgentCore Gateway sits
in front of every tool call, evaluated against Cedar — AWS's own deterministic,
formally-verified policy language.
The pattern every one of them converges on
1. A short-lived, per-agent credential — never a standing role or a secret shared across every agent instance.
2. The identity is resolved server-side, from the credential — never trusted from what the agent's own output claims to be.
3. The allow/deny decision is deterministic code (Rego, Cedar, an OpenAPI schema match) — not a second model asked to judge the first one's tool call.
4. Content-safety scanners (PromptGuard/CodeShield-style) are a SEPARATE, complementary layer — never a substitute for the authorization decision above.
JiMesh's own consumer-key tiers + INGRESS-DERIVED-ONLY headers + OPA capability gate is a working instance of the same shape.
